title: Semantic-variety reuse eventually repays ontology-specific tax
claim: Across at least three independently useful real domains, the shared Ontology Language/Engine/Toolchain reduces marginal adaptation effort for blind semantic changes/tasks enough to create a stable advantage over a strong conventional typed relational/event baseline without correctness or security regression.
null_hypothesis: Any local reuse is too small or rare to repay ontology-specific infrastructure, compiler, governance and cognitive tax; a conventional typed architecture scales equally well or better.
rivals: Apparent advantage comes from an unfairly weak baseline.
The advantage appears only in synthetic high-semantic-complexity tasks not representative of real project work.
Reuse benefits come from ordinary schema/code generation rather than ontology-specific semantics.
mechanism: A bounded meta-model plus reusable Engine/Toolchain should amortize common integration/governance/query/action machinery as semantic variety rises, flattening marginal domain/change cost.
scope: D1 Manufacturing, D2 Project Ontology and at least one later real D3+ project; blind change/query/policy/action/source-churn task corpus.
predictions: Marginal task-specific change effort grows more slowly for EOO than baseline as real domain count/semantic variety rises.
At least two independent task classes show material adaptation savings without lower correctness/security.
Ontology-specific recurring tax is measured explicitly and does not erase all adaptation gains in the supported region.
Benefits persist on real tasks, not only generated stress cases.
falsifiers: With N>=3 real domains, adaptation-cost slopes remain equivalent or favor baseline across preregistered task classes.
Savings disappear when equivalent code generation/caching/security tooling is provided to baseline.
Any material savings require sacrificing correctness, replay, security or maintainability.
Benefits occur only in synthetic benchmark cases outside declared realistic workload tiers.

experiment.summary: Blind cross-domain adaptation experiment extending Round 2 H15-H22 dimensions, gated until at least three real domains exist.
steps: Freeze both variants and task corpus generator before reveal.
Collect real D3+ domain(s) and preregister semantic-variety metrics.
Reveal blind tasks covering source churn, new relation/query, policy composition, action addition and interface reuse.
Measure files/LOC/components/migrations/bespoke tools/time-to-green/regressions plus runtime/maintenance tax.
Run correctness/security/replay oracles equally on both variants.
Fit marginal adaptation trends and report a trade-off frontier, not a weighted winner score.

oracle: Per-task independent correctness/security oracle plus Git-derived adaptation metrics and frozen measurement scripts.
baseline: Strong conventional typed relational/event architecture with equivalent schema generation, security, replay/audit requirements and competent optimization.

support_if: At least 3 independently useful real domains are included.
For at least 2 independent preregistered task classes, median normalized task-specific adaptation effort is <=75% of baseline while correctness/security are non-inferior.
Overall marginal adaptation-cost slope across real domains is <=75% of baseline slope with confidence/uncertainty reported.
A realistic workload tier exists where measured gains are not dominated by recurring ontology tax.
reject_if: With >=3 real domains, all preregistered task classes have adaptation ratio >=0.90 or favor baseline, or baseline has equal/lower marginal slope.
Any apparent supported savings disappear under fair baseline tooling or require correctness/security regression.
inconclusive_if: Fewer than 3 real domains exist, fewer than 30 blind tasks complete, or uncertainty spans both support and reject regions.
invalid_if: Task corpus, cost metric or baseline capability is changed after reveal to favor either variant without a new experiment version.

python_hypothesis_role.strategy: Generate adversarial variants of declared task shapes and source/schema mutations to broaden coverage; do not use synthetic property tests as the final real-domain trend evidence.
python_hypothesis_role.mutation_proof: Perturb cost accounting to ignore one variant's equivalent glue and verify fairness tests/reporting detect the asymmetry.

stop_conditions: Do not issue SUPPORTED/REJECTED trend verdict with fewer than three real domains; emit INCONCLUSIVE and wait for genuine domain evidence.
